rows.reading: the honest price of a gold LINE, measured: on PAPER the solve lands at L 55 (`oklch(55% 0.14 75)` = `#a06200`, 4.59 against paper), which the record flags as BELOW the L 60 floor at which a hue ~75 colour reads as gold — a bronze line that satisfies the arithmetic and the eye separately. On INK it lands at L 60 (`#b07100`, 4.59 against ink) and that one reads as gold. So the same hue is a gold on the dark tab and a bronze on the light one, and the reason is the bar, not the hue. Either way the row costs a token @theme does not have: `check:favicon` refuses `#a06200` and `#b07100` with "is not a token (nearest: --color-accent renders #a2432a)", and the candidate names are printed as candidates, not as tokens. At 16px the row is also QUIETER than the ratified pair it replaces — T1 measures 87 any / 61 at3 px, this row 90 any / 62 at3 but a max contrast of 4.59 against 17.15 — so a gold line buys prominence in HUE and pays for it in CONTRAST.
